# 1 Maccabees Chapter 15 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, 1 Maccabees 15 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/1MA_015_page_001.jpg

---

**1** Antiochus, son of King Demetrius, sent a letter from the islands of the sea to Simon the priest and ethnarch of the Jews and to all the nation.

**2** Its contents were as follows: "King Antiochus to Simon the great priest and ethnarch and to the Jewish nation, greetings.

**3** Since certain troublemakers have seized the kingdom of our ancestors, I intend to reclaim it and restore it to what it was before; and I have levied a great army and equipped warships,

**4** and I mean to march through the country to take vengeance on those who have ravaged our country and devastated many cities in our kingdom.

**5** Now therefore I confirm to you all the tax exemptions that the previous kings granted you, and whatever other gifts they gave to you.

**6** I also give you leave to mint your own coinage for your country.

**7** Jerusalem and the sanctuary are to be free; and all the weapons you have prepared, and all the strongholds you have built and occupy — let them be yours.

**8** Whatever is owed to the royal treasury and whatever shall be owed to it in the future — from this moment and forever, let all of it be released to you.

**9** And when we have reestablished our kingdom, we will bestow great honor on you, your nation, and your temple, so that your glory may be proclaimed throughout the earth."

**10** In the one hundred and seventy-fourth year Antiochus invaded the land of his ancestors, and all the forces rallied to him, leaving very few men with Trypho.

**11** Antiochus pursued him, and Trypho came fleeing to Dor by the sea.

**12** For he knew that trouble had closed in on him and his army had deserted him.

**13** Antiochus encamped against Dor with one hundred and twenty thousand warriors and eight thousand cavalry.

**14** He surrounded the city, and the ships closed in from the sea; he pressed the city hard from land and sea and allowed no one to enter or leave.

**15** Meanwhile Numenius and his companions arrived back from Rome, carrying letters to the kings and countries with the following contents:

**16** "Lucius, consul of the Romans, to King Ptolemy, greetings.

**17** Envoys from the Jews, our friends and allies, have come to us to renew their ancient friendship and alliance; they were sent by Simon the high priest and the Jewish people.

**18** They brought with them a golden shield of a thousand minas.

**19** We therefore resolved to write to the kings and countries that they should not harm them or make war against them, or their cities or their territory, and that they should not give assistance to those who fight against them.

**20** We also resolved to accept the shield from them.

**21** If, therefore, any treacherous men have fled from their country to you, hand them over to Simon the high priest so that he may deal with them according to their own law."

**22** He wrote similar letters to King Demetrius, and to Attalus, Ariarathes, and Arsaces,

**23** and to all the countries — Sampsames, Sparta, Delos, Myndos, Sicyon, Caria, Samos, Pamphylia, Lycia, Halicarnassus, Cos, Side, Aradus, Rhodes, Phaselis, Gortyna, Cnidus, Cyprus, and Cyrene.

**24** A copy of these letters was sent to Simon the high priest.

**25** King Antiochus made a second assault on Dor, continually throwing his forces against it and building siege engines; he cut Trypho off completely so that he could neither go out nor come in.

**26** Simon sent him two thousand picked troops to fight on his behalf, along with silver, gold, and much equipment.

**27** But he refused to accept them; he repudiated all the agreements previously made with Simon and became estranged from him.

**28** He sent his friend Athenobius to negotiate with Simon, saying: "You are holding Joppa and Gazara and the citadel in Jerusalem — cities that belong to my kingdom.

**29** You have devastated their territories and done great harm to the land, and you have seized control of many places in my kingdom.

**30** Hand over the cities you have seized and the tribute revenues from the places you have occupied outside the borders of Judea,

**31** or else pay five hundred talents of silver for the destruction you have caused, and another five hundred talents for the tribute of the cities. Otherwise we will come and make war on you."

**32** Athenobius the king's friend came to Jerusalem and, seeing the splendor of Simon — the sideboard with vessels of gold and silver, and his magnificent retinue — he was astonished; and he reported to Simon the king's demands.

**33** Simon replied: "We have not taken foreign land or seized foreign property, but only the inheritance of our ancestors, which our enemies had unjustly held for a time.

**34** We, seizing the opportunity, have held on to the inheritance of our ancestors.

**35** As for Joppa and Gazara, which you demand — these cities were causing great harm to our people and to our land. For them we are prepared to give one hundred talents."

**36** Athenobius gave him not a word in reply but returned to the king in anger; he reported Simon's reply and the splendor he had witnessed, and the king was furious.

**37** Trypho meanwhile boarded a ship and fled to Orthosia.

**38** The king appointed Cendebaeus as governor of the coastal region and gave him an infantry and cavalry force.

**39** He ordered him to encamp against Judea, to build up Kidron, to fortify its gates, and to make war on the people; while the king himself continued to pursue Trypho.

**40** Cendebaeus came to Jamnia and began to provoke the people, to raid Judea, and to seize and kill the people.

**41** He built up Kidron and stationed cavalry and troops there to make sorties along the roads of Judea, as the king had commanded him.
